title: Cover-based Jacobian index calculus does not beat sqrt(p) for prime-field curves (known algorithms)
question: Let E/F_p, p prime, #E = r prime, and pi: C -> E a cover of genus g with computable pullback. (A) For fixed g >= 2 (Diem/GTTD, O~(q^{2-2/g})) or plane degree d >= 4 (Diem, O~(q^{2-2/(d-2)})) the cost exponent is >= 1 > 1/2. (B) For g >= delta log q the L_{q^g}(1/2) cost (Enge–Gaudry) is q^{omega(1)}; for g >= (log q)^2 the L(1/3) cost (Enge–Gaudry–Thomé) exceeds sqrt(q) for large q. (C, heuristic) generic degree-1 factor-base index calculus on J_C costs >= ~q/20; formulas dip below sqrt(q) only for g = O(log q / log log q) where no theorem applies. (D) Pullback relations have disjoint supports and determine no individual factor-base logarithm. Missing ingredient: a factor base of size <= p^{1/2-eps} adapted to pi^*(E(F_p)) with fast decomposition.
rationale: Registered by PI from round-5 runs after PI reproduction of numerics.

next_action: Close as negative result for generic covers with known algorithms; revisit only if a structure-adapted factor base for pi^*E(F_p) is proposed.
notes: A proved from cited statements (Diem arXiv math/0606607, Diem JTNB verified; Gaudry 2000 and Enge–Gaudry regime unverified recollection); B conditional on regimes; C heuristic; D elementary. One sentence in Enge–Gaudry–Thomé intro read literally conflicts with C (treated as loose; unresolved). Cover t->t^d genus (3d-1)/2 (d odd), (3d-2)/2 (d even), generic h: 2d-1 (toy-checked). | ECDLP-18 decisive test (pre-registered; PI reproduced 2^10 run: identical except timing/argv): genus-2 double cover C: y^2 = f(w^2 + c) (degree-6 model; no degree-5 model since #E odd prime gives no rational 2-torsion); group law, pi^* homomorphism, [#J]D = 0 and #J = r * #E' checked. Degree-1 factor-base index calculus (variant B) recovered k on 12/12 curves but cost 1.0e5..3.9e9 total counted ops for p = 251..16381 (fitted exponent 2.52; Cantor-only exponent 0.97 ≈ 2 Cantor ops x p/2 relations) vs sqrt(p) = 16..128 and measured BSGS 26..217. Halving the factor base doubled Cantor cost. Pullback-only relations (variant A) never determine k after de-duplication (Lemma D confirmed); raw A succeeds only via rho-like collisions in E. Prediction "cost >= ~p" SURVIVES on tested domain (p <= 2^14); GTTD large-prime variants analytic only.
